newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statistics Norway revises up 1997 GDP, inflation.
newsitem.headline: Statistics Norway revises up 1997 GDP, inflation.

text.p: The Norwegian statistics office revised up the oil-rich country's 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) and inflation forecasts on Thursday.

Statistics Norway, in a quarterly report on key economic indicators, bumped up 1997 GDP growth to 3.0 percent from 2.3 percent and raised 1997 annual inflation forecasts to 2.3 percent from 2.2 percent.
Statistics Norway based its 1997 GDP revision to expansive fiscal policies and growth in petroleum investments.
Norway pumps about three million barrels of oil per day. It is the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia because it keeps only 150,000 barrels for domestic use.

And "The main reasons for the consumer price growth (in 1997) are tax policy amendments and higher electricity prices as well as domestic cost impulses stemming from higher wage growth," a statement said.
The government raised some indirect taxes in the revised 1997 state budget proposal on Friday.
And lack of snow and rain has driven up electricity prices to record highs in Norway, which relies almost exclusively on hydro power for energy.
However, the forecast for 1996 inflation growth was trimmed to 1.3 percent from 1.4 percent.

As a result of the higher expectations for oil and gas production, Statistics Norway also revised higher its 1996 GDP growth forecast to 4.8 percent from 4.3 percent and its 1997 current account surplus estimate to more than 71 billion Norwegian crowns ($10.92 billion).
"Along with higher oil prices, this also resulted in an upgrading of the current account balance," the statement said.

The 1997 current account surplus was now seen rising to 71.2 billion crowns from a forecast 64.6 billion in 1996. Statistics Norway's September forecast had the 1997 current account surplus swelling to 60 billion from 52 billion this year.
Mainland GDP growth, which excludes the thriving North Sea oil and gas sector, was also revised up to 2.7 percent from 2.4 percent in 1997.
Unemployment was expected to shrink to 4.0 percent next year compared with a previous forecast of 4.2 percent. In November, the jobless rate was 3.5 percent.

Statistics Norway's revisions follow upward revisions from the Finance Ministry on Friday. The Finance Ministry revised next year's budget surplus to 55.4 billion crowns from 40.9 billion crowns in the draft budget document.

The surplus, which was expected to be around 45.7 billion crowns this year compared with previous projections of 37.9 billion crowns, has swollen as oil prices have soared to five year highs. ($1=6.503 Norwegian Crown)
